newsitem.title: FINLAND: Outokumpu says Harjavalta copper halted.
newsitem.headline: Outokumpu says Harjavalta copper halted.

text.p: Finnish metals and mining group Outokumpu Oy said in a statement on Tuesday that damage to the copper flash furnace at its Harjavalta Metals unit had halted copper output on Monday, but had caused no injuries.

"Because of repair work on the copper flash furnace, the annual maintenance stoppage which was scheduled for early August will start immediately and the production is consequently also estimated to resume earlier than planned," Outokumpu said.
Due to the stoppage of copper production, the annual maintenance stoppage in the plant's nickel production would also be held earlier than originally planned, Outokumpu said.
The damage was probably caused by water leakage in the furnace, it said.
"The damages are not very big," Outokumpu spokeswoman Katarina Lybeck said by telephone, declining to give an estimate, but adding "the damages and the lost production are covered by insurance."
The loss in output would be about 4,000-5,000 tonnes of copper this year, Lybeck said.
Outokumpu's Harjavalta Metals smelter has an annual copper capacity of about 160,000 tonnes and an annual nickel capacity of about 40,000 tonnes, she said.
An explosion at the Harjavalta smelter at the end of June injured three employees, halted nickel production and caused damages of 20-30 million markka, Outokumpu said on June 30.
